Set the plan budget to 200ms for layout shifts and 300ms as the maximum for any transition.
Plan a helper that reads matchMedia for reduced motion and sets duration to 0 when it is true.

K-003960.example: rg finds 0 matches for prefers-reduced-motion, so the plan adds src/lib/motion.ts with a reducedMotion check. The budget is 200ms for layout shifts and 300ms maximum.
K-003960.check: rg prints the duration lines it finds, and the reduced-motion count is 0 or more with each match listed by file and line.
traps: Forgetting that reduced motion must set duration to 0, not just shorten it.
Choosing a 600ms fly for page-level transitions that users will feel as lag.
Adding the media query only in CSS and not in the Svelte transition calls.

steps.do: Find each blocks in the library folder.
Confirm the animate export exists in the svelte package metadata.
Record that flip from svelte/animate needs a keyed each block, and set its duration to 200ms in the plan.

K-003961.example: rg finds {#each items as item (item.id)} in src/lib/NavList.svelte, so the key is present and flip will work. grep shows the animate export in the svelte package.json.
K-003961.check: rg prints each lines that include a parenthesized key, and grep prints a line containing animate from the exports map.
traps: Using an each block without a key, so flip does nothing.
Importing flip from svelte/transition, which is the wrong module.
Animating a list whose items change identity on every render.

steps.do: Build the app so the baseline is measured on production output.
List the built javascript files to record the bundle count.
Run lighthouse against the preview server and print the performance results as json.
Record the cumulative layout shift value and set the plan limit at 0.1 or lower.

K-003962.example: npm run build exits with code 0, and lighthouse reports cumulative-layout-shift 0.02 for the preview server. The plan keeps layout shift under 0.1 after the motion change.
K-003962.check: npm run build exits with code 0, and the lighthouse json output contains a cumulative-layout-shift value.
traps: Measuring the dev server instead of the built preview, which gives different numbers.
Targeting a layout shift of exactly 0, which is not realistic for a layout with animation.
Skipping the baseline and comparing only against memory of an earlier run.

steps.do: Print the declared svelte version from package.json.
Ask npm for the installed svelte version tree.
Count prop declarations to confirm runes mode.
Count legacy slot elements; a count of 0 supports a Svelte 5 plan that uses {@render children()}.

K-003963.example: npm ls prints svelte@5.43.0 at the top of the tree, so the plan uses {@render children()} and $props(). rg -c slot reports 0 matches, which confirms no legacy slot usage.
K-003963.check: npm ls svelte prints one svelte@5.x.x or svelte@4.x.x line at the top of the tree, and rg -c slot prints a count of 0 or more.
traps: Mixing a slot element with runes in the same layout.
Trusting a Svelte 4 tutorial when the project is on Svelte 5.
Skipping npm ls and reading only the declared range in package.json.

steps.do: Create the plan file.
For each field, name the error element id, such as email-error.
Plan aria-invalid set to true when the field has an error, and aria-describedby set to the error id.
Set the error text color to meet a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against the card background.
Record the planned ids in the plan file and check each one appears.

K-003964.example: Email input gets id='email', aria-invalid={!!errors.email}, aria-describedby='email-error'; the error span has id='email-error'.
K-003964.check: grep -c '4.5:1' PLAN.md prints 1; grep -c 'error' PLAN.md prints at least the number of fields with an error element, e.g. 2 for two fields.
traps: Do not link aria-describedby to an id that is never rendered.
Do not use color alone to show an error; include text.

steps.do: List every transition declaration in the layout component.
Confirm the Transition name prop matches the CSS class prefix.
Type-check the component props so the Transition usage compiles.
Run the unit test that mounts the layout and asserts the 200ms transition duration.

K-003965.example: The sidebar uses name="slide" with .slide-enter-active set to transition: transform 200ms ease. The grep shows 200ms on line 42 and vitest reports 1 passed.
K-003965.check: The grep prints a line containing 200ms and vitest prints 'Tests 1 passed (1)'.
traps: Small models write .slide-enter instead of .slide-enter-from, .slide-enter-active, and .slide-enter-to, so the transition never runs. Vue applies all three classes at different phases.
Do not assume the duration in CSS equals the duration in JavaScript hooks. Check both.

steps.do: Find every prefers-reduced-motion media query in the source.
Run the Playwright test that emulates reduced motion and reads computed styles.
Assert in the test that the sidebar computed transition-duration equals 0s.
Confirm the test count shows zero failures.

K-003966.example: The layout sets transition-duration: 0.01ms inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce). The Playwright test with reducedMotion: 'reduce' reads 0s and reports 1 passed.
K-003966.check: The grep finds at least one media query line and the Playwright run prints '1 passed'.
traps: Small models set the media query on the wrong selector, such as the wrapper div, while the animated element is a child. Check the element that actually transitions.
Setting duration to 0 without also removing the transition property can still leave a delayed end event in Vue. Test the final state, not just the style.

steps.do: List every v-for in the layout component to find the lists.
Confirm each v-for has a :key bound to a unique id, not the index.
Run the test that adds and removes items and checks the DOM node count.

K-003967.example: The nav list uses v-for and :key="item.id" on a TransitionGroup with tag="ul". The test removes 1 of 5 items and asserts 4 li elements remain.
K-003967.check: The rg commands show a :key next to every v-for and vitest prints 'Tests 1 passed (1)'.
traps: Small models use :key="index", which makes items jump when the list changes. Use a stable unique id from the data.
Forgetting the tag prop on TransitionGroup renders a fragment and can break the layout wrapper. Set tag to the element you need.

steps.do: Run the Playwright frame test that records requestAnimationFrame timestamps during the transition.
Assert in the test that the longest frame gap is under 16.7ms.
Assert in the test that the whole transition finishes within 300ms.
Read the summary line printed by the test.

K-003968.example: The drawer open transition records 42 frames with a max gap of 14.2ms and a total of 280ms. The test passes because both numbers are under the limits.
K-003968.check: The Playwright run prints '1 passed' and the recorded max gap is 16.7ms or less.
traps: Small models measure only the transition end event and ignore frame timing. Record frames with requestAnimationFrame across the whole animation.
Headless browsers can differ from real devices, so state the browser and throttle setting in the test name.

steps.do: Build the production bundle so the audit runs on the real output.
Serve the built app on port 4173 in the background.
Run Lighthouse against the served page and save the JSON report.
Read the cumulative layout shift value from the report.

K-003969.example: The layout page reports a CLS numericValue of 0.02 after the sidebar slide completes. Since 0.02 is below 0.1, the layout passes.
K-003969.check: The jq command prints a number below 0.1, such as 0.02.
traps: Small models read CLS before the animation finishes, which hides shift that happens later. Wait for the transition to end before measuring.
A CLS of 0.1 or higher is a failure, not a warning. Report the number exactly.

steps.do: Search the layout components for transition declarations and read every match.
Search the layout components for animation declarations and read every match.
Search the templates for inline style bindings and read every match, because they can also set width or height.
Rewrite each match so it animates only transform or opacity, and keep the original duration.
Run the test suite and confirm it exits with status 0 and reports 0 failing tests.
Search the components for any remaining geometry transitions and confirm the search prints no lines and exits with status 1, which means 0 matches.
steps.cmd: rg -n -e transition.*width -e transition.*height -e transition.*top -e transition.*left src/components

K-003970.example: A drawer used transition: width 300ms and was rewritten to transform: translateX with 300ms. The final rg command prints no lines for the drawer file and exits with status 1.
K-003970.check: The final rg command prints no lines and exits with status 1, and npm test exits with status 0 and reports 0 failing tests.
traps: Small models count the search as proof but ignore inline style bindings like :style with width values. Also search the template for those.
Changing the property to max-width still triggers layout. Use transform and opacity for motion.

steps.do: Confirm the toast store module exports its toasts store.
Create the unit test file for the validation path.
Run only that test file with Vitest in run mode.
Check the test counts store entries and asserts the length is exactly 1 after one invalid submit.

K-003971.example: Submitting the signup form with an empty email calls the validate function once, which pushes one toast with level error into the toasts store. The Vitest run then reports 1 passed with the store length equal to 1.
K-003971.check: npx vitest run prints 'Tests 1 passed (1)' and the exit code is 0.
traps: Small models assert that a toast is visible instead of counting store entries, which passes even when duplicates exist.
Do not submit the form twice in the test, because a second submit adds a second toast and makes the count 2.

steps.do: Confirm svelte-check is installed as a dev dependency.
Run svelte-check against the project tsconfig and treat any error as a failure.
Read the final summary line, which must show 0 errors for the toast and form files.

K-003972.example: The ToastMessage type restricts level to success, error, or info, and the signup form passes an error payload that matches it. svelte-check then reports 0 errors across the project.
K-003972.check: The last line reads 'svelte-check found 0 errors' and the command exits with code 0.
traps: Small models type the toast payload as any to silence errors, which hides a wrong level value.
A run that prints warnings but no errors is not a pass for this check; the summary must show 0 errors.

steps.do: Check the toast container sets an aria-live attribute in its source.
Run the Playwright spec that submits the signup form with empty fields.
Confirm the spec asserts the live region contains 'Email is required' and that the role is status or alert.

K-003973.example: The spec clicks Create account with empty fields, then expects the status region to contain 'Email is required' with aria-live set to polite. The run prints 1 passed.
K-003973.check: Playwright prints '1 passed' and grep prints a line number for the aria-live attribute in the toast files.
traps: Small models check the toast text but skip the live region, so the message stays silent for screen reader users.
Setting aria-live to assertive for every level is too loud; success and info toasts should stay polite.

steps.do: Start the built app with the Vite preview server on a fixed port.
Submit the invalid form in the browser to show the error toast, then scan the signup page with axe for WCAG 2 AA rules.
Find the error text color token in the toast styles so you can record the foreground value.
Confirm there are no color-contrast violations and that the error text measures at least 4.5:1.

K-003974.example: Error text #b91c1c on a #ffffff background measures about 6.5:1, above the 4.5:1 minimum for normal text. The axe scan reports 0 color-contrast violations.
K-003974.check: axe prints 0 violations and exits with code 0, and the measured ratio is 4.5:1 or higher.
traps: Small models scan before the toast appears, so the error text is not in the DOM and the scan passes falsely.
The 3:1 ratio applies only to large text; normal toast text needs 4.5:1.

steps.do: Find the 5000ms duration in the toast component.
Create the Vitest file that uses vi.useFakeTimers and checks the toast count at two times.
Run the dismiss test file.
Confirm the test asserts the count is 1 at 4999ms and 0 at 5000ms, and calls vi.useRealTimers in afterEach.

K-003975.example: Toast.svelte sets the duration to 5000, and the test advances the clock by 4999ms to see count 1, then by 1ms to see count 0. The run reports 1 passed.
K-003975.check: Vitest prints 'Tests 1 passed' and grep prints the line that contains 5000.
traps: Small models advance the clock by exactly 5000 and assert removal, which misses a bug where the toast disappears early.
Forgetting vi.useRealTimers in afterEach leaks fake timers into other tests.

steps.do: Confirm the ESLint config file exists at the project root.
List the files in the toast directory to see which components will be linted.
Run ESLint on the toast directory with the Svelte plugin rules.
Confirm the output reports 0 problems, and fix any icon-only button that lacks an aria-label.

K-003976.example: A close button in Toast.svelte with only an icon lacks a label, and the fix adds aria-label='Dismiss notification'. Rerunning ESLint reports 0 problems.
K-003976.check: npx eslint exits with code 0 and prints no problem lines.
traps: Small models add role='alert' to every element to silence lint, which floods screen readers with announcements.
A clean ESLint run does not prove contrast or timing; those need axe or a test.

steps.do: Count the list items in the test fixture to see how many delays are needed.
Set the delay step to 40ms per item index.
Cap the largest delay at 320ms.
Write each delay as an arbitrary value such as [transition-delay:80ms] for index 2.
Confirm no delay value in the source exceeds 320ms.

K-003977.example: Index 0 gets no delay, index 4 gets [transition-delay:160ms], and index 8 and beyond are capped at [transition-delay:320ms].
K-003977.check: rg prints only values from 0ms to 320ms, such as transition-delay:160ms, and no value above 320ms.
traps: Using delay-1000 on long lists so the last item takes seconds to appear. Forgetting that the cap must hold for lists longer than 8 items.

steps.do: Confirm Tailwind v4 is installed in the project.
Check that the CSS entry file imports Tailwind.
Plan starting:opacity-0 and starting:translate-y-2 on each new li.
Pair the starting classes with transition-[opacity,transform] duration-200 ease-out.
Add motion-reduce:transition-none to the same li so reduced-motion users get no fade.
Check that the starting variant appears in the source once per planned li class.

K-003978.example: New li elements use starting:opacity-0 starting:translate-y-2 with transition-[opacity,transform] duration-200 ease-out, so each row fades up over 200ms on insert.
K-003978.check: npm ls tailwindcss prints a 4.x version, and grep -rn starting: src prints one line per planned li class.
traps: Using starting: in a Tailwind v3 project where the variant does not exist. Writing transition-all, which animates layout properties and causes extra reflow.

steps.do: Find the files that render list elements.
Count the list item lines in the list component.
Find every existing transition utility in the source.
Confirm the Tailwind major version, since v3 uses tailwind.config.js and v4 uses @theme in CSS.
Check that every duration class is 200ms or less by listing the duration values in the source.
Write the file paths and current classes into the plan before editing.

K-003979.example: TodoList.tsx has 4 li elements that use transition-colors and no duration class, so duration-* must be added. package.json lists tailwindcss 4.x, so the plan targets @theme and starting: variants.
K-003979.check: grep -c prints 4 for src/components/TodoList.tsx, and grep tailwindcss package.json prints a line such as "tailwindcss": "^4.1.0". The rg duration check prints no value above duration-200.
traps: Assuming a tailwind.config.js exists in a v4 project. grep -c counts matching lines, not rendered items, so a line with two li tags counts once.

steps.do: List the duration classes already used in the project.
Confirm the theme does not override the duration scale.
Pick duration-150 for hover feedback and duration-300 for enter animation.
Record a maximum total list animation time of 300ms.
Check that no list class uses duration-700 by searching for it.
Check that no list class uses duration-1000 by searching for it.

K-003980.example: Rows use duration-150 on hover and duration-300 on enter, so the list finishes entering within 300ms. The rg checks find no duration-700 or duration-1000 classes.
K-003980.check: rg prints no lines and exits with code 1 for duration-700 and for duration-1000, which is the expected result when no slow durations exist.
traps: Using arbitrary values like duration-[437ms] that drift from the scale. Enter animations longer than 500ms make long lists feel slow.

steps.do: Find list items that use animate or translate classes.
Count the existing motion-reduce variants.
Add motion-reduce:translate-y-0 and motion-reduce:animate-none to each animated li.
Use motion-safe for movement classes so they apply only when reduced motion is not requested.
Verify the motion-safe count matches the animated items.
Confirm each animated row finishes within 200ms by listing its duration classes.

K-003981.example: TodoList.tsx has 3 li elements with translate-y-2 and animate-fade. Each gets motion-reduce:translate-y-0 and motion-reduce:animate-none, so the reduced-motion count for that file is 3.
K-003981.check: grep -rc motion-reduce src/components/TodoList.tsx prints 3, matching the 3 animated li lines. The duration listing shows no value above duration-200 for animated rows.
traps: Adding motion-reduce only to the wrapper and not the item that moves. Using motion-reduce:transition-all when only opacity should change.

steps.do: Find every transition-all class in the list files.
Allow only transform and opacity in list transitions, using transition-transform or transition-opacity.
Replace any height or margin animation with translate or scale utilities.
Keep each row at least 44px tall using min-h-11, which is 2.75rem.
Confirm the row height class is min-h-11 or larger.
Count width transitions that remain in the source.
Count height transitions that remain in the source.

K-003982.example: Row hover uses group-hover:translate-x-1 with transition-transform duration-150 instead of transition-all, and rows keep min-h-11 for a 44px tap target.
K-003982.check: rg -c prints 0 for width and height transitions, and rg -n "min-h-11" src prints a line for each row class, confirming the 44px minimum.
traps: Animating height to expand rows, which causes layout shift. Shrinking the hit area below 44px while the row scales down.

steps.do: Fix the base body size at 1rem (16px) and the ratio at 1.25.
Compute the scale steps from index -1 to 3 using the ratio.
Mark the smallest step as caption-only, since it falls below 1rem.
Create the styles folder that will hold the token file.

K-003983.example: The node command prints 0.800 1.000 1.250 1.563 1.953, so the tokens become 0.8rem, 1rem, 1.25rem, 1.563rem, and 1.953rem. The 0.8rem step (12.8px) is reserved for captions and is not used for body text.
K-003983.check: The node command prints exactly 0.800 1.000 1.250 1.563 1.953, and mkdir -p exits without error.
traps: Small models often mix px and rem values in the same scale.
Do not pick a ratio without writing it down, because later tokens will not match.
Body text must be 1rem or larger; a smaller step is only for captions.

steps.do: Start the Vite dev server so the layout can be scanned.
Scan the running page with axe for WCAG 2 AA violations, including color contrast.
Record the minimum contrast of 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text in the plan.
List the existing color tokens so each text and background pair can be checked.

K-003984.example: Axe reports 2 color-contrast violations for muted gray text (#9aa0a6) on white, which measures about 2.5:1. The plan changes that token to a darker gray that meets 4.5:1.
K-003984.check: The axe command reports 0 color-contrast violations and exits with code 0; any failing pair is listed by selector and ratio.
traps: Small models often check one background and miss the others in the layout.
Large text needs only 3:1, but normal body text needs 4.5:1.
Guessing a hex value without measuring it wastes a pass; run the scan first.

steps.do: List every padding declaration in Vue components to see which values are in use.
List every line-height declaration to see which values are in use.
Compute spacing steps as multiples of 0.25rem for the chosen indices.
Set body line-height to 1.5 and heading line-height to 1.2 in the plan.

K-003985.example: The node command prints 0.25rem 0.5rem 0.75rem 1rem 1.5rem 2rem, which becomes the spacing tokens --space-1 through --space-4 plus --space-6 and --space-8. The plan replaces the 13px and 15px padding values found by grep.
K-003985.check: The node command prints exactly 0.25rem 0.5rem 0.75rem 1rem 1.5rem 2rem, and the grep output shows the old padding values to replace.
traps: Small models often keep odd pixel values like 13px instead of mapping them to the grid.
Do not set line-height with px, because unitless values scale with font size.
Count the existing values before choosing the scale, not after.

steps.do: Start the demo app on port 5173 in its own terminal so the contrast spec can load it.
Run the contrast spec in Chromium, which reads computed colors for the toast title and body in each theme.
Confirm the spec asserts a minimum ratio of 4.5:1 for normal text, not a looser 3:1 value.

K-003986.example: The dark toast uses text #e6edf3 on background #161b22, which the spec computes as 14.6:1 and passes. If a token change drops the dark title to 3.1:1, the spec fails with 'expected 4.5, received 3.1'.
K-003986.check: The Playwright run prints '2 passed' and exits 0, and the grep prints the line containing 4.5.
traps: Many models check only the light theme and forget the dark theme needs its own run.
Lowering the threshold to 3:1 to get a pass is wrong because toast body text is normal size and needs 4.5:1.
Running the dev server in the foreground blocks the shell, so start it in the background first.

steps.do: Run the theme unit tests for the Toast component with Vitest in run mode, not watch mode.
Check that the test renders Toaster inside ThemeProvider with the theme set to dark.
Type-check the project so the theme value stays a union of light, dark and system.

K-003987.example: The test renders ThemeProvider with theme dark and expects the toast background to resolve to rgb(22, 27, 34), which passes. If the provider value is ignored, the test fails with 'expected rgb(22, 27, 34) but received rgb(255, 255, 255)'.
K-003987.check: Vitest prints 'Tests 3 passed (3)' and the type check prints nothing and exits 0.
traps: Running npx vitest without run starts watch mode and stalls the session.
Asserting only a class name misses broken CSS variables, so assert the resolved color.
Testing the light theme alone does not prove the system option works.

steps.do: Run the system scheme Playwright spec, which emulates prefers-color-scheme dark and light and reads the toast background.
Confirm the spec sets colorScheme to dark and not only light.
Confirm the Toast stylesheet has a prefers-color-scheme media query for the dark tokens.

K-003988.example: With the OS set to dark, the spec emulates colorScheme dark and reads the toast background as rgb(22, 27, 34), which matches --toast-bg in the dark block. If the media query is missing, the same spec fails with 'expected rgb(22, 27, 34) but received rgb(255, 255, 255)'.
K-003988.check: Playwright prints '2 passed' and exits 0, the grep shows at least two colorScheme lines, and the stylesheet count is 1 or more.
traps: emulateMedia must run before page.goto or the first paint uses the light theme.
Setting data-theme alone does not prove the system path works.
A media query that sets only light values leaves dark-mode users on light colors.

steps.do: Start the dev server in the background so the demo page is reachable.
Scan the demo page forced to dark theme with axe, checking WCAG 2 AA rules and exiting nonzero on any violation.
Scan the same page forced to light theme so the two results can be compared.
Type-check the project to confirm the theme types still compile.

K-003989.example: The dark scan reports 0 color-contrast violations and exits 0, and the light scan also reports 0 violations. If a dark token drops below 4.5:1, the dark scan lists color-contrast and exits 1.
K-003989.check: Both axe runs exit 0 with 0 violations, and the type check prints nothing and exits 0.
traps: axe scans only rendered DOM, so the toast must be open on the page before the scan runs.
Omitting --exit makes a failing scan look like success.
Running axe before the dev server starts returns a connection error, which is not a pass.

steps.do: Count hex color literals in the toast stylesheet; the expected count is zero.
Count rgb color functions in the toast stylesheet; the expected count is zero.
Count var calls that read toast tokens; the expected count matches the six tokens in the theme file.
Run the contrast spec, which checks each toast text and background pair in light and dark themes; every pair must reach a 4.5:1 contrast ratio.

K-003990.example: The first grep prints 0, the rgb grep prints 0, and the var grep prints 6, matching the six toast tokens in the theme file. The Playwright run reports 0 failed tests, with the lowest pair at 4.5:1 or higher. A hardcoded border of #ffffff would make the first count 1 and fail the check.
K-003990.check: The hex and rgb counts print 0, the var count prints 6, and the Playwright contrast run exits with 0 failed tests and no pair below 4.5:1.
traps: grep -c exits with status 1 when the count is zero, which a model may wrongly read as an error.
Hardcoded colors often hide in border or box-shadow lines, so check those too.
A hex value in a comment still raises the count, so remove it or explain it.
Quote the '#' and var patterns, because an unquoted # starts a shell comment and unquoted parentheses are a syntax error.

steps.do: Count every toast token declaration in the global theme file; six tokens in each of two blocks gives 12.
List the toast token lines with line numbers to confirm each name appears under both the root and the dark selector.
Confirm the dark theme selector appears exactly once in the file.
Run the token spec, which reads each toast token's computed value under both themes and fails if any resolves to an empty value or to the light value in dark mode; the run must report 0 failed tests.

K-003991.example: The file has 12 lines declaring --toast- tokens, six under :root and six under the dark selector. The dark selector count is 1, so the dark block exists once. The Playwright run reports 6 tokens checked per theme and 0 failed tests.
K-003991.check: The first grep prints 12, the dark selector grep prints 1, and the Playwright token run exits with 0 failed tests across all six tokens in both themes.
traps: Counting only the light block misses tokens missing from the dark block.
A token declared in one block only makes var() silently fall back to the light value, so the grep counts alone cannot catch it.
grep -c counts lines, so two declarations on one line count as one.
grep -c exits with status 1 when the count is zero.
Playwright exits with status 1 on any failed test, so read the reported counts, not only the exit status.

steps.do: Confirm the built entry file exists before timing it.
Record the start time in milliseconds.
Run the built CLI help command to measure bare startup.
Record the end time in milliseconds.
Write the budget into PLAN.md: spinner after 200ms and a hard step limit of 3000ms.

K-003992.example: The start reads 1762300000123 and the end reads 1762300000431, so startup took 308ms. That is above the 200ms spinner threshold, so the loader must appear during startup.
K-003992.check: stat prints the file details with exit status 0, and the two date lines differ by a value in milliseconds that the plan records.
traps: Small models use date +%s, which gives seconds, and then compare the result to millisecond budgets. Always use %3N for milliseconds.

Count matches per file to set a baseline for the plan.
Confirm ink-spinner is already a declared dependency.

K-003993.check: The rg -c output shows a non-zero count per file, the package.json grep prints a line containing ink-spinner, and the final rg -c prints 1 for 80ms.

steps.do: Confirm ratatui is a dependency in Cargo.toml.
Find existing Gauge or Paragraph widgets in the source.
List direct dependencies to confirm the crossterm backend.
Create the plan file.

steps.do: Confirm the plan file records the 100ms redraw interval.
Confirm the project compiles before writing any code.

K-003994.example: cargo tree --depth 1 lists ratatui and crossterm, so the Gauge uses the crossterm backend. The plan redraws the Gauge every 100ms with a ratio between 0.0 and 1.0, and rg -c prints 1.
K-003994.check: The rg output shows a ratatui line in Cargo.toml, cargo tree lists crossterm, the 100ms count is 1, and cargo check ends with a Finished line.

steps.do: Find existing key bindings in the onboarding package.
Find existing run_worker calls that the cancel must stop.
Check the Python version available for Textual.
Create the plan file.
